subject: Re: Incident communications + post-incident summaries
body:
From: Alex Kim <alex.kim@fintrustbank.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Priya Desai <priya.desai@fintrustbank.com>
Date: Wed, Jun 12, 2024 at 4:08 PM PT
Subject: Incident communications + post-incident summaries

Hi Naomi,

Thanks again for the demo earlier today.

As part of our enterprise review, could you confirm Redwood’s incident communication practices?

Specifically:
1) During an incident, do you post updates on a public status page? If so, what’s the expected cadence and level of detail (region/component)?
2) Do you publish post-incident summaries (external-facing) as a standard practice, or only upon request? What timelines do you commit to?
3) For Dedicated/VPC deployments, is there a separate comms path (e.g., direct email/Slack channel) vs only public status?

We’re trying to align expectations internally before we move forward on the commercial path.

Best,
Alex Kim
Director, Platform Engineering
FinTrust Bank

From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwoodinference.com>
To: Alex Kim <alex.kim@fintrustbank.com>
Cc: Priya Desai <priya.desai@fintrustbank.com>
Date: Wed, Jun 12, 2024 at 5:02 PM PT
Subject: Re: Incident communications + post-incident summaries
Attachments: Redwood_Incident_Comms_Status_Page_Overview_2024-06.pdf

Hi Alex,

Absolutely — sharing what we do today and what we’re formalizing as we expand our status-page transparency.

1) Public status page + cadence
- Yes, we maintain a public status page: https://status.redwoodinference.com
- When we have a customer-impacting incident, we post an initial update as soon as we confirm impact and then continue to update as we learn more.
- The status page is the canonical source for broad platform incidents (Hosted API / Console / control plane). For partial degradations, we aim to be specific about symptoms (e.g., increased 5xx, elevated latency, streaming disruptions) and scope (e.g., a subset of regions/routes/model families), but the exact component granularity varies by incident.

2) Post-incident summaries
- Today: for Sev1/major incidents, we can provide an external-facing summary upon request (typically shared via email). This is distinct from our internal postmortem and is reviewed to ensure we don’t disclose sensitive/security details.
- Standardization: we’re in the process of rolling out a consistent, customer-facing post-incident summary format (impact, timeline, root-cause category, mitigations/prevention). Our target is to publish/share these within a few business days for major incidents.

3) Dedicated/VPC comms path
- For Dedicated and Private/VPC customers, we typically use both:
  a) Public status page for issues that broadly affect shared control-plane/product surfaces
  b) Direct customer comms (email and, for some accounts, a shared incident Slack channel) for account-specific impact/mitigations (e.g., capacity constraints, pinned model versions, specific routing policies)

I attached a 1-pager summarizing the above. If helpful, I can also walk your team through a recent sanitized example of an external incident summary so you can see the level of detail.

Ava (cc’d) leads part of our customer comms policy work and can confirm the summary approach/timelines in a way that’s consistent with what we can commit to contractually.

Best,
Naomi Feldman
Account Executive, Enterprise
Redwood Inference
naomi.feldman@redwoodinference.com

From: Ava Chen <ava.chen@redwoodinference.com>
To: Alex Kim <alex.kim@fintrustbank.com>
Cc: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwoodinference.com>, Priya Desai <priya.desai@fintrustbank.com>
Date: Thu, Jun 13, 2024 at 8:26 AM PT
Subject: Re: Incident communications + post-incident summaries

Hi Alex,

Adding a bit of precision on post-incident summaries.

- We do publish real-time incident updates on our public status page during incidents.
- For post-incident communication, our intent is to provide a consistent external-facing “post-incident summary” for major customer-impacting incidents. This is derived from the internal postmortem but is intentionally scoped/redacted to avoid security-sensitive details and customer-specific information.
- For enterprise customers, we can also provide additional context directly (under NDA where appropriate), depending on the nature of the incident and the deployment model.

Naomi can coordinate an example (sanitized) and, if your procurement/security team wants it, we can also outline what we consider in-bounds vs out-of-bounds to share externally.

Regards,
Ava Chen
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Incident communications + post-incident summaries

Thanks Naomi + Ava — super helpful.

Two quick follow-ups:
1) If an incident is limited to streaming responses (vs non-streaming completions), would that be reflected distinctly on the status page? We’ve had providers mark “API Degraded” broadly, which doesn’t help our routing decisions.
2) For region-specific impact (e.g., us-east only), do you call out region scope on the status page updates?

If the answer is “it depends today but improving,” that’s fine — we just need to document what to expect.

Best,
Alex
